summary.text: 本 is a tree, 木, marked at its lower part to indicate the root. The root sense is associated with later recorded uses meaning base, foundation, source, and basis, though their exact development is unclear.

formation.text: Indicative: 木 depicts a tree, and a mark below or across its lower part identifies the root. The transmitted explanations differ on whether that mark is 一 or 丅.

components.text: 木 depicts a tree, providing the plant context for the root indication. In this construction it is pictorial and semantic, not phonetic.
In one transmitted analysis, 一 is the lower mark indicating the tree’s root. Another reading identifies the mark as 丅; the available accounts do not show that one form developed from the other.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style illustration shows a tree-like form crossed by a lower horizontal mark. It is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. Early inscriptional evidence remains unsettled: one record lists a bronze example that another does not display, and a proposed oracle-bone precursor is disputed; these do not establish a secure sequence of graphic change.
The transmitted Shuowen explanation describes 木 with a lower mark. Its readings differ on whether the mark is 一 or 丅, without establishing a sequence between those forms.

uncertainties.text: The earliest inscriptional form and date remain unresolved. The reported bronze graph’s reading and meaning are unsettled, and the proposed oracle-bone identification is disputed.
Root, trunk, base, foundation, source, and basis are recorded meanings, but the precise pathways from the root sense to abstract, documentary, or other uses are not established.

senses.text: The transmitted Shuowen explanation gives 本 the sense ‘root’; a cited Book of Odes passage uses it for a plant’s lower part or root. The passage’s composition date is unresolved.
A cited Zhuangzi passage records 本 for a tree trunk. Its first occurrence and precise relation to the root sense are undated.
Dictionary citations include base and foundation uses, such as the Analects phrase 君子務本，本立而道生. They do not date when this sense arose.
Source, cause, and basis are recorded meanings, but their precise development from root or foundation is undated.
Current definitions include root, origin, source, and basis; this list does not establish their chronology.

A Japanese lexical account proposes that 本 meaning ‘original’ or ‘source’ came to refer first to an exemplar manuscript and then to books generally. This proposed Japanese word history is separate from the documented Chinese senses and from the character’s graphic origin.

developments.text: Both root and foundation are documented; an extension from a plant’s base to a figurative basis is plausible, though its transition and chronology are not demonstrated.
Source and basis uses are recorded alongside foundation, but the precise development and dates are not shown.

limitations.text: The cited literary passages and dictionary entries document uses but do not establish exact first-attestation dates or a complete chronology of semantic development.
The earliest archaeological attestation is unresolved, as is the reading of the reported bronze example.

items.period: Han Shuowen seal-script model; digital image uploaded 2016
items.caption: This seal-script-style form of 本 has a tree-like upper structure and a horizontal mark across its lower part. In the traditional analysis, 木 represents a tree and 一 marks its base, indicating the root. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.
items.alt: Bold black seal-script-style graph on white: a tree-like form with a horizontal stroke crossing its lower trunk.
items.selection_reason: It visibly illustrates the lower mark central to the traditional explanation of 本 as a root indicator, while its modern redraw status is made clear.

limitations.text: The image is a modern redraw of a seal-script-style form, not an ancient artifact. The early inscriptional history of 本 remains unsettled: a bronze example is listed by one source but not displayed by another, and an oracle-bone identification is disputed.
